title: Financial Controller Salary: Converting Hourly Rates to Annual Pay in Australia
description: Learn how to convert a financial controller salary from hourly to annual using the 38-hour week, plus tax, super, and the National Minimum Wage vs award rates.
salarySummary: A financial controller salary is typically well above the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, but understanding the conversion from hourly to annual using a 38-hour week is essential for comparing offers.

faqs.q: How do I convert an hourly rate to an annual salary for a financial controller role?
faqs.a: Multiply the hourly rate by hours per week (usually 38 for full-time) and then by 52 weeks. For example, $60 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $118,560 per year. This assumes no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or salary sacrifice. Use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool for quick calculations.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates for financial controllers?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour ($1,004.90 per week for 38 hours). Award rates are higher and set by the Fair Work Commission for specific industries. Financial controllers are often covered by the Clerks Award or a Professional Employees Award, which have higher minimum rates. Award minimum wages increased by 4.75% from 1 July 2026. Always check the applicable award for your role.

faqs.q: Does the financial controller salary include superannuation and casual loading?
faqs.a: Superannuation (12% of ordinary earnings) is paid on top of the base salary, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Casual loading of 25% applies to casual employees, added to the base hourly rate. For example, a casual financial controller on $50 per hour would receive $62.50 per hour including loading. Super is then calculated on the ordinary hours component. See our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page for more details.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Financial Controller Salary in Australia

When evaluating a **financial controller salary**, it is common to see offers expressed as an hourly rate, a fortnightly wage, or an annual package. To compare these fairly, you need a reliable conversion method that accounts for standard hours, tax, and superannuation. This guide explains the process using the 38-hour week, the National Minimum Wage, award rates, and the latest figures from the Fair Work Commission and the Australian Taxation Office.

### The Basic Conversion Formula

The core formula for converting an hourly rate to an annual salary is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

For full-time employees, the standard week is 38 ordinary hours. For example, if a financial controller earns $60 per hour:

- Weekly: $60 × 38 = $2,280
- Fortnightly: $2,280 × 2 = $4,560
- Annual: $2,280 × 52 = $118,560

This calculation assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, and no salary sacrifice. It is a starting point for comparing job offers. Use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool to run your own numbers.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The **National Minimum Wage** sets the legal floor for award/agreement-free employees. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. This rate applies to adult employees not covered by an award or agreement. For casual employees, a 25% loading applies, making the minimum $33.05 per hour.

However, most financial controller roles are covered by an **award** – typically the Clerks Award (MA000002) or the Professional Employees Award (MA000020). Award rates are higher than the National Minimum Wage and include specific classifications with higher minimum pay points. From 1 July 2026, award minimum wages increased by 4.75%. For example, a Financial Controller under the Clerks Award may have a minimum hourly rate of $35–$50 depending on experience. Always check the relevant pay guide for your specific classification.

If you are offered a **financial controller salary that is award-free, the National Minimum Wage applies. But in practice, most employers pay above award to attract skilled professionals.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

**Casual loading** is paid on top of the base hourly rate. For casual financial controllers, the 25% loading compensates for lack of paid leave and leave loading. The formula still uses the base hourly rate – never enter a rate that already includes casual loading. Our [timesheet](/topics/casual-loading) page explains how to calculate the total casual rate.

**Superannuation** is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top of the base salary. The super guarantee applies to all ordinary earnings up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For a financial controller earning $120,000 per year, super is $12,000 paid on top. This is not deducted from the salary; it is an additional cost for the employer.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Once you have the annual gross figure, you can estimate tax using the 2026–27 resident tax scale:

- $0–$18,200: nil
- $18,201–$45,000: 15% on excess over $18,200
- $45,001–$135,000: 30% on excess over $45,000
- $135,001–$190,000: 37% on excess over $135,000
- $190,001+: 45% on excess over $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (with possible reductions for low income). For a financial controller salary of $118,560, the tax estimate (excluding Medicare) would be:

- Tax on first $18,200: $0
- Tax on $18,201–$45,000: $4,020 (15% of $26,800)
- Tax on $45,001–$118,560: $22,068 (30% of $73,560)
- Total tax: $26,088
- Medicare levy: $2,371 (2% of $118,560)
- Net annual: $118,560 – $26,088 – $2,371 = $90,101

Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator for a more detailed estimate.

### Putting It All Together

When comparing a **financial controller salary** offer, follow these steps:

1. Confirm the base hourly rate (exclude casual loading if casual).
2. Multiply by 38 hours × 52 weeks to get annual gross.
3. Add superannuation (12% on top) if comparing total package.
4. Check the applicable award or the National Minimum Wage as a floor.
5. Estimate tax and Medicare to understand net income.

Remember that the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) is only the starting point. Most financial controllers earn well above award rates, but understanding the conversion ensures you can compare offers accurately. For award-specific rates, refer to the [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman.
